title: Part Twenty-Eight: Cathars, Crusade and Inquisition

sections.brief: The Good Men (c.1143-1350): name coined by opponents; Bogomil roots (Cosmas c.970, Interrogatio Iohannis); bishops (Albi c.1165, Saint-Félix 1167, eleven by 1200); two principles (absolute vs mitigated), fallen-angel souls, docetic Christ, cross refused; credentes and perfecti, melioramentum, convenenza, consolamentum (Lyons Ritual: Lord's Prayer, 'not lie, not swear, not kill', laying on of hands), endura (few late cases, disputed); women perfectae; Gui's account of their critique of clergy, sacraments, vernacular scripture; no tithes, no oaths; surviving texts; Moore/Pegg vs Taylor/Rist/Sackville debate; Pays cathare and Grail myths. Figures: compare (Roman vs Cathar church)

Innocent III's missions; Castelnau murdered Jan 1208; crusade with Holy Land indulgences (Lateran IV c.3); Béziers 22 July 1209 (bishop's list of 222; Amalric's 'almost 20,000' vs Tyerman/Marvin; Caedite eos only in Caesarius 1219-23); Carcassonne, Minerve 140, Lavaur, Muret 1213, Louis VIII, Meaux/Paris 1229; Montségur 16 March 1244 (c.210-215 burned, Bertrand Marty; voluntary walk and treasure unverified); toll: no reliable total (200k-1m unsourced); genocide debate Pegg vs Lerner. Figures: time

Constantine's edict as precedent (link vt21); Ad abolendam 4 Nov 1184; Vergentis 1199; Lateran IV c.3; Toulouse 1229 (vernacular scripture banned to laity); Excommunicamus 1231; papal inquisitors 1231-33; Talmud 1239/1242; Ad extirpanda 15 May 1252 (torture, property in thirds); Gui's sentences (Théry: 916 decisions, c.45 burned); Fournier register 1318-25 (578 interrogations, five burned; Montaillou); Bélibaste 1321; Holy See's 2000 and 2004 statements.
